families.name: Foundation
families.description: Illustrative mandatory foundation family used to exercise the resolver before production architecture profiles are introduced.

families.name: Example architecture choice
families.description: Illustrative mutually exclusive architecture family demonstrating multi-option selection.

families.name: Example add-ons
families.description: Illustrative independently composable capability family.

families.name: Identity and device authorization architecture
families.description: Versioned alternatives for authorizing devices that can receive end-to-end protected content. Product conformance requires one when identity/device management is in scope.

families.name: Pairwise end-to-end encryption
families.description: Complete asynchronous one-to-one session profiles combining a published prekey initialization protocol with a ratcheting protocol. Product conformance requires one when pairwise E2EE is in scope.

families.name: Group end-to-end encryption
families.description: Complete group-messaging architecture profiles for asynchronous multi-device groups. Product conformance requires one when group E2EE is in scope.

families.name: Manual key verification
families.description: Versioned manual verification profiles that bind an out-of-band safety number/QR representation either to stable account-root identities or to the complete active device-key sets.

families.name: Key transparency
families.description: Versioned Key Transparency deployment profiles that detect inconsistent or rolled-back cryptographic identity-directory views.

families.name: Backup and recovery
families.description: Mutually exclusive E2EE backup/recovery architectures covering no recoverable backup, user-secret recovery, and hardware/HSM-assisted recovery.

families.name: Metadata privacy
families.description: Complete metadata-privacy profiles ranging from strict collection/retention minimization through sender-hidden delivery to relay-partitioned sender-hidden submission.

families.name: Contact discovery
families.description: Privacy-preserving discovery profiles for learning which known identifiers or exact handles correspond to discoverable E2EE users without exposing a client's address book to the service.

families.name: Attachments and file encryption
families.description: Chunked authenticated file-encryption architecture for E2EE attachments, including key distribution, streaming/range verification, substitution/replay resistance, and deletion semantics.

families.name: Real-time media
families.description: End-to-end encrypted real-time audio/video profiles using RFC 9605 SFrame with either sender-key distribution over an existing E2E control channel or MLS-derived conference keys.

families.name: Secret storage and hardware protection
families.description: Local protection profiles for device identity keys, protocol state, recovery material, and other E2EE secrets using OS keystores, hardware-isolated key managers, external hardware tokens, or an encrypted software fallback.

families.name: Transport security
families.description: TLS 1.3 transport profiles for ordinary authenticated transport and RFC 10024 post-quantum/traditional hybrid key agreement, usable over stream TLS or QUIC without weakening application-layer E2EE.

families.name: Native and web client security
families.description: Native and web client security. Product conformance requires an applicable profile when this capability is in scope.

profiles.notes: Resolver fixture only; not a production cryptographic architecture.
Illustrative profile only.
Illustrative profile only.
Illustrates exact version pinning and provisional opt-in.
Illustrates deterministic dependency expansion.
Illustrates symmetric incompatibility semantics from a one-sided declaration.
Illustrates explicit experimental opt-in.
Illustrates a profile that can exist historically in the catalog but can never resolve as conformant.
Stable client-controlled account cryptographic root authorizes device enrollment, rotation, and revocation.
Existing active devices authorize device-set changes without a separate persistent account-root signing key.
A strict majority of eligible active devices authorizes device-set changes.
Classical asynchronous X3DH Revision 1 initialization followed by Double Ratchet Revision 4. Does not claim post-quantum confidentiality.

Transitional PQXDH Revision 3 initialization with classical Double Ratchet Revision 4. PQ confidentiality claims are limited by the declared quantum threat model and do not imply post-quantum authentication or post-quantum PCS.
PQXDH Revision 3 followed by the Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet with ML-KEM Braid from Double Ratchet Revision 4. Provides a pure PQ ratchet option without the classical Double Ratchet hedge.

Recommended hybrid profile: PQXDH Revision 3 plus Triple Ratchet Revision 4, combining the classical Double Ratchet and SPQR/ML-KEM Braid. Does not claim post-quantum authentication because current PQXDH authentication remains classical.
Recommended standards-based group profile using MLS 1.0 (RFC 9420), with authenticated membership epochs, forward secrecy, and post-compromise security.

Efficient Sender-Keys-style group profile using pairwise E2EE to distribute per-sender chain state, registered KDF/AEAD/signature algorithms, and mandatory full rotation on membership changes. Does not claim automatic PCS.
Simple O(n) group architecture that encrypts each group message independently to every current recipient device using a selected E2EESA pairwise profile; no shared group content key.

Manual verification binds a canonical safety digest to the two client-controlled account-root public keys. Device changes authorized beneath an unchanged verified root do not automatically invalidate the root verification.
Manual verification binds a canonical safety digest to the complete active device-key sets for both parties. Any active-device or verified key-set change invalidates the prior verification.
Single-party IETF Key Transparency deployment using durable client monitoring state plus anonymous or peer gossip/fork-detection channels.
Recommended stateful-client deployment using independent third-party auditor attestations, bounded auditor lag, owner monitoring, and client checkpoint continuity.
Recommended where clients are ephemeral or vulnerable to state loss: an independent manager operates the log while the service operator authenticates label updates and detects forks.
No recoverable copy of protected content or content-decryption keying material is retained outside currently authorized E2EE endpoints. Maximizes confidentiality at the cost of recoverability.
Client-side encrypted backup with a fresh random backup data key protected by an Argon2id-hardened user-held recovery secret. Server storage alone cannot recover plaintext.

Defense-in-depth recovery: the Argon2id user-secret envelope is additionally protected by a non-exportable hardware/HSM wrapping key and authenticated, rate-limited release path. Hardware/service compromise alone remains insufficient to decrypt the backup.

Baseline metadata-minimization profile. Collect only delivery/abuse metadata that is explicitly required, keep retention bounded, and prohibit durable social-graph construction from ordinary message delivery records.

Adds sealed-sender-style delivery so the service routes to a recipient without learning the authenticated sender identity from ordinary message submission. Network source address remains visible to the service unless another transport hides it.

Strongest E2EESA 0.1 messaging-metadata profile: sender-hidden application envelopes submitted through an independent Oblivious HTTP relay/gateway partition so the message service does not receive the client network address.

No address-book discovery. Users connect only through exact user-supplied handles, QR codes, invite links, or equivalent discovery tokens. The service never receives the client's local contact set, but the explicit queried handle may be visible to the service.

Recommended cryptographic private membership discovery using RFC 9497 VOPRF over normalized identifiers plus a versioned directory membership structure. The VOPRF server learns neither queried identifier inputs nor VOPRF outputs; online evaluation rate limits constrain enumeration.

Confidential-compute discovery in which the complete contact set is encrypted to an attested enclave/TEE that computes the intersection and returns only results. The host/service must not observe plaintext query identifiers; assurance depends on attestation, implementation review, and the declared TEE side-channel model.

Fresh 256-bit key per attachment; AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 recommended, AES-256-GCM-SIV allowed; independently authenticated fixed-size chunks using a unique 96-bit prefix||counter nonce, an E2EE-delivered authenticated manifest, and strict no-key-in-URL/storage metadata rules.

RFC 9605 SFrame with a fresh sender-owned base key distributed over a pre-existing authenticated E2EE control channel. Best fit for 1:1 and smaller groups; every active sender rotates on membership changes.
RFC 9605 SFrame using its MLS exporter/KID construction over the E2EESA RFC 9420 group profile. Recommended for multiparty conferences and membership churn.

Uses the native OS keystore/keychain to hold a non-exportable or OS-confined wrapping/private key and protects mutable E2EE secret state in an authenticated encrypted vault. Hardware backing is used when available but is not required or claimed by this profile.

Requires verified hardware-isolated non-exportable key material in Secure Enclave, StrongBox/TEE, TPM 2.0, HSM, or equivalent hardware. Secret state remains client encrypted; attestation and authorization evidence must prove the selected hardware boundary.

Uses an external hardware token/HSM exposed through PKCS #11 or an equivalent reviewed interface. The device vault is encrypted under key material that cannot be exported from the token and token removal can intentionally make local secrets unavailable.

Fallback for platforms without a trustworthy keystore. A high-entropy generated secret or Argon2id-hardened user secret protects the local encrypted vault. This profile does not claim non-exportability or protection against a fully compromised live endpoint.
RFC 9846 TLS 1.3 using ephemeral traditional ECDHE groups. Suitable where hybrid PQ/T TLS is unavailable or not required. Does not claim post-quantum confidentiality.

RFC 9846 TLS 1.3 with an RFC 10024 PQ/traditional hybrid group. X25519MLKEM768 is the default; P-256/ML-KEM-768 and P-384/ML-KEM-1024 are available for deployments with FIPS-oriented requirements. This profile does not by itself claim PQ authentication.
Independently installed signed releases, authenticated update metadata, artifact-bound code transparency and native isolation.
CSP/SRI hardened browser delivery with independent transparency monitoring; origin still controls executable code. No malicious-origin prevention claim.
An independently installed verifier authenticates the complete web executable closure before execution and rejects unapproved releases.
Relays, queues, object stores, backups, KMS and subprocessors cannot decrypt application E2EE or independently authorize recipients.
No exported telemetry or durable diagnostics; local manual debugging is separate.
Explicit opt-in bounded diagnostic codes; no content, keys, identifiers, pseudonyms or raw crash dumps.
Pure central-Laplace aggregate counts with user-lifetime adjacency, contribution bounds and cumulative privacy-budget evidence; collector access remains explicit.
SSDF 1.1 aligned development controls with independent review, exact-source test/scanning gates and time-bounded risk handling; no high/critical release waivers.
Complete immutable dependency inventory, validated SBOM, authenticated SLSA build provenance, isolated signing and independently reproduced release bytes.
Independent external-interface/property/fuzz/adversarial assessment, without internal software or key-lifecycle proof claims.
Independent source/internal-state review with property, fuzz, adversarial and bounded protocol-model evidence.
Combined external and internal assessment with per-profile method/threat/property coverage and no unresolved counterexamples.
